summary: Prometheus Monitoring is a web app that turns 23 years of NASA FIRMS fire hotspots from MODIS and VIIRS into one consistent weekly record of burning activity. The two sensors do not see the same fires. VIIRS detects many small fires that MODIS misses, so simply adding their counts makes burning look like it jumped when VIIRS launched in 2012. Our app measures each sensor’s detection rate against VIIRS S-NPP for every grid cell and calendar month, then combines all sensors into one comparable record. For any Indian state or grid cell it shows a burning activity calendar, the typical year, the critical burning windows, whether the season is shifting, and unusually active weeks. Across India, raw counts jump 6.7 times at the sensor change. After harmonization the jump is 1.04 times. When we hide a year of VIIRS data and rebuild it from MODIS alone, the yearly total is off by 2.2%, against 82% for raw MODIS counts. This gives responders, scientists and land managers a record they can compare across the whole period.
details:
Live app: https://advikj1604-cmyk.github.io/Burn-Calendar/

What it does
Burn Calendar shows a calendar heatmap of burning activity, one row per year and one column per week, from 2003 to 2025. You can pick any Indian state from a menu or click a single grid cell on the map. For the chosen area it finds the main burning windows, how the season start is moving, the long-term trend, and weeks far above normal. Users can also load their own FIRMS CSV files for any other region.

How it works

  1. We keep presumed vegetation fires and drop low confidence detections.
  2. We count detections per 0.5 degree grid cell, per sensor, per week.
  3. For weeks when two sensors were both flying, we measure each sensor’s detection rate relative to VIIRS S-NPP, per cell and per calendar month. Cells with little data lean on the regional value.
  4. Weekly activity is the total count from all sensors flying, divided by the sum of their detection rates. The unit is VIIRS S-NPP equivalent detections.
  5. Weeks when only MODIS Terra was flying (before mid 2002) are left out, because its morning pass sees too few fires to scale up safely.

How we checked it
For each of 13 years with both records, we hid that year’s VIIRS data, refitted the rates without it, and rebuilt the VIIRS record from MODIS alone. For all of India the rebuilt yearly total is off by 2.2% (median). For Punjab it is 7.1%. Raw MODIS counts are off by 82% and 77%.

What we found for Punjab
The main burning window is 8 October to 18 November and holds 74% of a typical year. The season now starts about 8 days later per decade. Burning in this window is down about 10% per decade. 2025 was 72% below the median year. MODIS makes 1 detection for every 5.3 that VIIRS S-NPP makes.

Benefits
Responders can see the critical weeks for their area. Scientists and land managers get a record that can be compared across the MODIS and VIIRS eras without a false jump.

Limits
Activity means satellite detections, not burned area. Fires that MODIS cannot see at all cannot be recovered. Results get noisier for small areas, and a single quiet grid cell can be off by more than 25%. Fires lit after the afternoon satellite pass are missed by every sensor.

Tools
JavaScript, HTML and CSS for the app, which runs fully in the browser with no server. Python for preparing the FIRMS files. Hosted on GitHub Pages. We used the AI assistant Claude to help design the method and write the code, and this is noted in the repository README.
